title: CSS
body:
[[CSS Selectors]]

---

*Cascading Style Sheets* — the language that says how the [[HTML]] should look. HTML carries
structure and semantics, CSS carries appearance, and [[JavaScript]] carries behaviour; keeping
those three apart is the whole point of having three languages.

A rule is a selector plus a block of property/value declarations:

```css
#first p.box {
	color: white;
	background-color: green;
}
```

**Cascading** is the conflict-resolution part of the name: when several rules apply to the
same element, the winner is decided by specificity (an [[ID Selector]] beats a
[[Class Selector]] beats an [[HTML Selector]]), then by source order. Inline `style=` beats
all of them, which is why [[Modifying Documents]] prefers toggling a class over setting
`node.style` directly.

The reason this matters beyond styling: `document.querySelector` takes a CSS selector string,
so the selector syntax is also the query language for the [[DOM]]. See [[Selecting Nodes]].
